First, I'll parse the SVG path data to determine the shape it draws. The path consists of multiple line commands ("L") connecting points:

- Start at (62.25, 27.53)
- Line to (52.77, 26.60)
- Line to (47.60, 32.11)
- Line to (41.50, 34.36)
- Line to (33.95, 29.67)
- Line to (41.91, 21.19)
- Line to (49.46, 13.14)
- Line to (62.25, 27.53) — closing back to start

Counting the distinct vertices:
1. (62.25, 27.53)
2. (52.77, 26.60)
3. (47.60, 32.11)
4. (41.50, 34.36)
5. (33.95, 29.67)
6. (41.91, 21.19)
7. (49.46, 13.14)
8. Back to (62.25, 27.53) — same as first point

So the path has 7 distinct vertices before returning to the start: vertices 1 through 7 listed above. A polygon with 7 sides is a heptagon.

Checking geometric principles:
- The path is closed (ends at start point).
- All segments are straight lines (no curves).
- 7 vertices mean 7 sides.
- Not a triangle, quadrilateral, pentagon, hexagon, or octagon (those have 3, 4, 5, 6, or 8 sides).
- Not a circle (no curves), kite (4 sides), rectangle (4 sides), sector (circular segment), or single line.

Thus, it matches a heptagon.

Final answer: (B)
